subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers be permanently denied access to legacy ownerless session rows, or should doctor/migration assign or repair ownership before the fail-closed rule lands?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes upgrade behavior for pre-ownership rows; repository source cannot establish whether existing ownerless plugin sessions must be migrated, deliberately locked out, or temporarily supported.

options.title: Fail closed after migration
options.body: Add a doctor or migration path for attributable legacy rows, then reject any remaining ownerless rows at runtime.

options.title: Fail closed immediately
options.body: Accept that existing plugin-runtime workflows may lose patch access to all legacy ownerless rows and provide a documented, proven operator recovery path.

options.title: Temporary compatibility policy
options.body: Preserve ownerless access only through an explicit, time-bounded compatibility rule with removal criteria and focused tests.

recommendation.title: Fail closed after migration
recommendation.body: Add a doctor or migration path for attributable legacy rows, then reject any remaining ownerless rows at runtime.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on the session accessor and SQLite storage boundary makes this the strongest available owner signal for the upgrade and security-policy choice.
